## What this accepts

The maintainer accepted these residuals on 2026-11-08 rather than close them with stricter inputs:

- The reviewer reads the pull request's comments, which can include Melian's and Codex's findings. A review of record that repeats a Melian finding after reading it counts as independent agreement in the comparison record, so recall measured against it can read high.
- The builder chooses the model by judging whether its own change is a trust surface. A missed trust implication gets Sonnet where Opus was due.
- The coordinator's spot checks are the only control on both. A review the spot check finds steered, or run on the wrong model, is sent back for a fresh one.
The review of record's brief, its independence and its model. Who runs each review. The rules for marking a pull request ready and queueing it.

- `<model>`: Opus 5.5 when the change touches a trust surface, otherwise Sonnet 5.5. A trust surface is anything that decides what code runs with credentials, what a head can read or write, who may post or dismiss, what blocks a merge, or what survives a crash or a second host. Sandboxes, workflows, tokens, the store, the lease, and the verdict and its status all count.

# The three reviews run first on one head

Status: ruled by the maintainer on 2026-11-27, in the coordinator's session. The coordinator proposed it; the maintainer asked for the draft and agreed its text that day.

## Problem

Every pull request gets Codex's adversarial review, a Melian round and the Claude review of record. AGENTS.md ran them one after another: Codex first, then its fixes, then a round, then its fixes, then the review of record. Each reviewer saw different code. A defect Codex found was fixed before Melian's round ran, so the round could neither find it nor miss it.

Example: the maintainer's parity loop needed to know which defects each reviewer finds. For the three pull requests it measured, [#613](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/613), [#619](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/619) and [#623](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/623), the coordinator had to run each reviewer again, blind, on one old head, and build each defect list by hand. About forty pull requests merged between 2026-11-04, the date of the newest comparison record, and 2026-11-27 with all three reviews posted and nothing that could compare them.

## Choice

The three reviews run first on one commit: the first head the builder pushes with its gate green, or with CI green on it where the gate cannot run. The builder starts all three together, pushes no fix until all three have reported, and names the commit in its report as the first reviewed head.

After that head, each fix pass gets a Melian round and nothing else. Codex's review and the review of record run once, on the first reviewed head. The maintainer ruled this on 2026-11-28, in the coordinator's session: "we've reached a level of recall that I'm satisfied with only using All 3 models for that first code review to build up our parity database. Following fixes, lets just use the melian review." Choice: the builder of a pull request runs Codex's adversarial review on its own branch, and its own Melian rounds through the `melian round` workflow, before the first round and after each fix pass. It posts the review's JSON and its findings in the pull request's report, and fixes from them. The coordinator still reads the verdicts, runs the round a dismissal or the comparison record needs, marks the pull request ready and queues it.

Amends: [docs/decisions/2026-10-15-review-loop-convergence-rules.md](2026-10-15-review-loop-convergence-rules.md), who runs the review of record

The maintainer ruled on 2026-11-08 that the builder starts the review of record, from [the review-of-record brief](../review-of-record.md), instead of the coordinator.

## Why

The review of record was the last review the coordinator ran by hand. Each one waited for the coordinator's machine and attention, and today three of them queued behind the host's load. Nothing technical kept it on the host once a cloud session's gate passes, which [pull request #329](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/329) brings. A cloud VM is a better place for probes than the coordinator's machine: it is isolated and competes with nothing.

What the coordinator gave the review was independence. It wrote each brief from the issue, the rulings and the diff, never from the builder's reasoning. A fixed brief keeps that: the builder fills in the pull request's number, its base and head commits, and the model, and adds no analysis of its own. The fresh-context agent reads everything else from GitHub and the repository, so the builder's view never steers what it attacks.

## The rule

- The builder starts a fresh-context agent with the brief and four values: the pull request, its base and head commits, and the model, after Codex's review and the first Melian round.
- Sonnet 5.5 runs it, and Opus 5.5 on a trust surface, as the brief defines one.
- The builder posts the report and its JSON unchanged, and fixes each finding with a failing test first. A disputed finding is answered on the pull request, never dropped.
- The coordinator imports the JSON into the comparison record and spot-checks a sample of reviews. A spot check that finds a review was steered, or skipped what the brief requires, sends the pull request back for a fresh one.
- The brief changes only through a pull request, so a builder never edits the instructions its own reviewer follows.

`Amends: <target link>, <scope>` declares a narrow change to an active target. Effective amendments are only its active Amends sources. The index renders the target as `[ACTIVE; amended by Y]`. The design lens reads the target and its effective amendments; where they conflict, the amendment wins. An amendment alone retires nothing.

If B amends A and C supersedes B, A stays active without B as an amendment. B is history, and the lens receives no conflict authority for it. Two active amendments of one target both stand, including when one also amends the other.

An Amends edge to an inactive target invalidates the graph, even when its source is inactive. Refuse it as a cycle is refused. Name the target, say it is inactive, and name every active successor reachable through Supersedes edges to amend instead. The graph already gives Supersedes precedence when one source declares both edge kinds to the same target; that pair creates no amendment edge. Separate sources amending and superseding one target still leave an invalid amendment target.

`Supersedes:` means whole retirement. Restate every surviving clause in the replacement. Every new or changed edge draws one P3 `guardrail/supersession-drop` notice on the declaring file, even when every clause is restated. The notice says which target is retired and asks the author to restate what survives. Uncarried sentences are evidence, never the trigger. Exact text cannot distinguish a rewrite from a lost obligation.

Use the ten most recent eligible merged pull requests after 2026-10-06T00:00:00Z. Every merged pull request in this repository after that instant is eligible, whether its comparison exists or not. A missing record or pending adjudication in that window blocks retirement. Require at least one adjudicated valid in-scope distinct shadow finding; zero findings leave recall undefined and keep both shadows running.

Recall must still reach 0.75. Count each distinct valid in-scope finding once across both shadows, and each pull request once across rounds. Noise, duplicates and out-of-scope findings stay outside the denominator. Fewer than ten eligible merged pull requests keep the shadows running. Missing comparisons stay absent; never reconstruct them.

The root policy still stores the window size and recall threshold. The fixed start and non-zero finding floor are part of this decision. The retirement result in melian compare stats remains a follow-up to [pull request #72](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/72).

This tightens the criterion the maintainer supplied. The fix-pass brief explicitly requests the change; the maintainer must confirm it before either shadow is retired. Neither reviewer is retired by this decision.

- The design lens is to replace Codex's adversarial review. Both run on the same head every round until Codex's review meets [the shadow retirement rule](docs/decisions/2026-10-06-shadow-retirement-merged-window.md) and the maintainer retires it.

AGENTS.md line 202 says neither runs after the first head, while line 161, which this change left alone, says both run on the same head every round. The next design-lens round, or a review of record that takes its rules from the base `docs/decisions/` as its brief requires, judges a later PR against the still-active 2026-11-05 text. It then flags a builder who skipped Codex on a fix pass, or misses that a fix pass on a trust surface got no shadow review at all, because the active decisions say it did. No supersession-drop notice was drawn for this change, because it declared no edge.
